column3: This process map is based on the officially-promulgated but non-mandatory phases specified in England and Wales Civil Procedure Rules J-codes / Precedent H / Precedent S / Practice Direction 3E. Where there are minor wording differences between these sources, one version has been chosen and others appear in the Alternative names column. Four additional unofficial phases have been added for topics which in practice often require substantial work and expense: Amendments and requests for further information; Summary determination; Related proceedings for challenges, appeals and enforcement; and Detailed assessment of costs. The Scope clarifications noted in the Assumptions column summarise the PD3E table of inclusions and exclusions.

Covers exchange of information and positions before court proceedings, including compliance with any applicable pre-action protocol. Settlement activities are included in the Settlement phase, not here. PD3E inclusions: pre-action protocol correspondence; investigating the merits of the claim and advising client; settlement discussions, advising on settlement and Part 36 offers; all other steps taken and advice given pre action. PD3E exclusions: any work already incurred in relation to any other phase.
column4: complete pre-action protocol forms, correspond with other party to provide information, indicate intention to commence proceedings
column6: Pre-action protocol correspondence completed, letter of claim sent and response received

column3: Covers initiation of court proceedings and exchange of statements of case. Also note that amendments and requests for further information are split into a separate phase (phase 7). PD3E inclusions: preparation of claim form; issue and service of proceedings; preparation of particulars of claim, defence, reply; considering opposing statements of case and advising client; Part 18 requests; updating schedules of loss; amendments to statements of case.
column4: acknowledge service, correspond before action / claim, file initial court documents, issue proceedings, pay initial court fees, prepare and review pleadings, prepare answer, prepare complaint, prepare counterclaim, prepare crossclaim, prepare defence, prepare initial court documents, prepare reply, prepare statement of claim, receive service, serve proceedings / complaint / process / request
column5: acknowledgement of service, answer / defence, claim form, counterclaim / crossclaim, letter before action / claim, reply, response to letter before action / claim
column6: Claim issued and served, statements of case exchanged

column3: Covers establishment of procedure, timetable and budget, and resolution of procedural issues arising during the case. In noslegal, this phase is assumed to include all case management matters and interim applications, with the exception of applications to determine all or part of the case summarily (see Summary determination, phase 11). PD3E inclusions: completion of directions questionnaire; arranging a CMC; reviewing opponent's budget; correspondence to agree directions and budgets; preparation for and attendance at the CMC; finalising the order; any further CMC built into the directions. PD3E exclusions: preparation of costs budget for first CMC.
column4: appear at or attend case management conference / CMC / costs and case management conference / CCMC, apply for disclosure or document production, apply for freezing order, apply for interim injunction, apply for interim measures, apply to consolidate, apply to join, establish procedural timetable, prepare directions questionnaire / DQ
column5: costs budget, directions, directions questionnaire / DQ, directions ruling, agreed budget, agreed directions, roadmap for case
column6: Directions questionnaire filed, CMC attended, directions and costs budget approved

column3: Covers preparation and exchange of documentary evidence. PD3E inclusions: obtaining documents from client and advising on disclosure obligations; reviewing documents for disclosure, preparing disclosure report or questionnaire response and list; inspection; reviewing opponent's list and documents; correspondence about scope of disclosure; consulting counsel in relation to disclosure. PD3E exclusions: applications for specific disclosure; applications and requests for non-party disclosure.
column4: advise on factual legal and evidential issues, gather analyse and disclose documentary evidence, deduplicate documents, establish keywords, review documents, select ediscovery / edisclosure platform, use technology-assisted review / TAR
column5: advice on factual, evidential or legal issues, document list / list of documents, documentary evidence

column3: Covers preparation and exchange of factual witness statements. PD3E inclusions: identifying witnesses; obtaining statements; preparing witness summaries; consulting counsel about witness statements; reviewing opponent's statements; applications for witness summaries. PD3E exclusions: arranging for witnesses to attend trial (included in Trial preparation).
column4: advise on factual legal and evidential issues, interview factual witnesses, prepare factual witness statements, review factual witness statements
column5: Witness statements, witness summaries, record of review of witness statements

column3: Covers preparation and exchange of expert reports and arrangement of experts' meeting. PD3E inclusions: identifying and engaging suitable expert(s); reviewing draft and approving report(s); dealing with follow-up questions of experts; considering opposing experts' reports; conferences with counsel relating to expert evidence; meetings of experts. PD3E exclusions: obtaining permission to adduce expert evidence (included in CMC); arranging for experts to attend trial (included in Trial preparation). This phase applies only where expert evidence has been ordered.
column4: arrange for experts to meet, instruct expert witnesses, prepare agenda for meeting of experts, review draft and final reports of expert witnesses
column5: instructions to expert, expert report, agenda for meeting of experts, record of review of expert report
column6: Expert reports exchanged, experts' meeting held and joint statement produced

column3: Covers amendment of statements of case and requests for further information under CPR Part 18. This is an unofficial noslegal phase, not derived from J-codes / Precedent H / Precedent S. It is split out from Statements of case to enable better tracking of when the initial pleadings phase is complete, and for better mapping to other forms of dispute resolution. This phase applies only where amendments or Part 18 requests arise.
column4: prepare amendments, review amendments, prepare request for further information, respond to request for further information, review further information provided
column5: amended defence, amended counterclaim, amended particulars of claim, amended reply, request for further information, further information
column6: Amendments or requests for further information resolved

column3: Covers resolution of how the trial will be conducted. PD3E inclusions: bundle; preparing and agreeing chronology, case summary and dramatis personae (if ordered); completing and filing pre-trial checklists; correspondence to agree directions; preparation for and attendance at the PTR. PD3E exclusions: assembling and/or copying the bundle.
column4: prepare bundle for pre-trial review / PTR, prepare case summary, prepare chronology, prepare dramatis personae, prepare for pre-trial review / PTR, complete pre-trial checklist, attend or appear at pre-trial review
column5: pre-trial review / PTR bundle, chronology, case summary, dramatis personae, pre-trial checklist, up to date budgets, up to date case plan
column6: Pre-trial checklist filed, PTR attended, trial directions confirmed

column3: Covers practical arrangements for trial and any final evidential issues before trial. PD3E inclusions: trial bundles; witness summonses and arranging for witnesses to attend trial; any final factual investigations; supplemental disclosure and statements (if required); counsel's brief fee; pre-trial conferences and advice from counsel; pre-trial liaison with witnesses. PD3E exclusions: assembling and/or copying the trial bundle; counsel's refreshers.
column4: agree brief fee and refreshers, issue and serve witness summonses, liaise with witnesses, make supplemental disclosure, prepare trial bundle, arrange pre-trial conferences and advice
column6: Trial bundle filed, witness arrangements confirmed

column3: Covers presentation of the substantive issues in the case to the court with scope for live questioning of witnesses and obtaining decisions on those issues and costs. PD3E inclusions: solicitors' attendance at trial; all conferences and other activity outside court hours during the trial; attendance on witnesses during the trial; counsel's trial refreshers; dealing with draft judgment and related applications. PD3E exclusions: preparation for trial (included in Trial preparation); counsel's brief fee.
column4: argue factual legal and procedural issues, examine witnesses, make submissions, prepare witness examination, represent party at trial
column5: skeleton arguments, notes produced during trial

column3: Covers applications for strike-out, summary judgment, or trial of a preliminary issue. This is an unofficial noslegal phase, not derived from J-codes / Precedent H / Precedent S. It is separated from Case management because it can take substantial time and cost if attempted, and involves resolution of the substance of the case rather than purely procedural matters. This phase applies only where a summary determination application is made.
column4: argue factual legal and procedural issues, make submissions, prepare for and appear at summary judgment hearing, prepare for and appear at trial of preliminary issue, prepare for and appear on strike-out application
column5: skeleton arguments, notes produced during hearing
column6: Application for summary determination issued, judgment on summary determination obtained

column3: Covers seeking an agreed resolution of substantive issues in the case. This is a standing phase that runs throughout the matter. PD3E inclusions: conferences and advice from counsel in relation to settlement; work directed to settlement negotiations and ADR including Part 36 and other offers and advising the client; approval of settlement; drafting settlement agreement or Tomlin order; advice to the client on settlement. PD3E exclusions: advice included in the pre-action phase.
column4: analyse BATNAs, analyse settlement options, draft and negotiate settlement agreement, engage in ADR, engage in alternative dispute resolution, engage in early neutral evaluation, engage in ENE, engage in med-arb, engage in mediation, engage in negotiated dispute resolution, engage in NDR, engage in non-court-based dispute resolution, engage in NCBDR, engage in other forms of non-binding dispute resolution, engage in settlement discussion, explore settlement options, hold without prejudice discussion, identify common ground, identify key decision-makers for settlement, implement agreed settlement terms, make and analyse offer or counter-offer, negotiate confidentiality terms for settlement discussions, obtain necessary approvals for settlement, prepare position paper, prepare Tomlin order, present position in settlement meeting, select a neutral party for mediation or facilitation
column5: consent order, mediation position paper, mediation settlement agreement, settlement agreement, settlement offer, Tomlin order
column6: ADR or settlement discussions commenced, settlement agreement or Tomlin order agreed (if applicable)

column3: Covers enforcement of the outcome of the case and challenges to the outcome, including appeals and detailed assessment of costs. This is an unofficial noslegal phase, not derived from J-codes / Precedent H / Precedent S. It applies only where appeals, enforcement action or other related proceedings arise.
column4: appeal, apply for or resist recusal, apply to or resist setting aside of decision, challenge jurisdiction or forum or venue, enforce or resist enforcement, seek permission to appeal / PTA
column5: application for permission to appeal / PTA, court application, decision on jurisdiction or forum or venue challenge, enforcement order, freezing order, notice of appeal, recusal decision, registration of award
column6: Permission to appeal obtained or refused, appeal or enforcement proceedings concluded

column3: Covers detailed assessment of costs following a costs order. This is an unofficial noslegal phase, not derived from J-codes / Precedent H / Precedent S. It is separated out because detailed assessment can take on a life of its own (a species of satellite litigation) in England & Wales litigation. This phase applies only where costs are formally assessed rather than agreed or summarily assessed.
column4: attend and appear at detailed assessment hearing, prepare comments / points of dispute on receiving party's bill of costs, prepare bill of costs
column5: bill of costs, comments on bill of costs, costs certificate, final costs certificate, interim costs certificate, points of dispute, Points of Reply, Joint statement, advocacy
column6: Bill of costs served, detailed assessment hearing completed, costs certificate issued
